html:
The Missouria are a Native American people of the lower Missouri River, whose main villages stood near the mouth of the Grand River in what is now the state of Missouri. The river and the state are named after them.

They spoke Chiwere, a Siouan language shared with the Otoe and Iowa; the three peoples share a tradition of coming west from the Great Lakes. They farmed maize and hunted bison and deer.

French traders from New France reached them in the late 1600s. In the 1700s smallpox and attacks by the Sauk and Meskwaki devastated them, and by the 1790s most survivors had joined the Otoe. The two peoples were moved to Oklahoma in 1881 and form the Otoe-Missouria Tribe today.
